title: Pick up every beeper
brief:
There are beepers on some squares of the corridor, but not all of them. Pick up every beeper. Karel should finish at the end wall.

Tested on two corridors of different lengths, with beepers in different places.

Be careful with the last square: a loop that moves and then checks will miss it.

vocabulary.gloss: run the indented lines only when the condition is True
True if Karel's square has at least one beeper
the problem of the first or last item being different from the others — here, the last square
a line that does nothing. It keeps a function valid while it is still empty — replace it with real commands

worlds.name: Ten squares, beeper on the first

starterCode:
def main():
    pass  # replace this line with Karel's commands
hints: On each square, ask if beepers_present(). If yes, pick_beeper(). Then move. Put that inside while front_is_clear().
A loop of 'check, then move' stops when Karel reaches the last square — but Karel never checks that last square. Do one more check after the loop.
Shape: while front_is_clear(): [if beepers_present(): pick_beeper()] [move()] — and then the same if, once more, after the loop ends.
